summary:
When publication succeeded but the original feed readback failed, a later proof can recover evidence without another pack, push or tag change. The cited Algorithms implementation joins the exact original source/tag/run/attempt, native artifact digest and publication-state evidence, then downloads the organization feed archive and requires whole-file equality with the original retained package. Normalized payload equality and a fresh public-feed consumer answer different questions; a public signature may change raw archive bytes. Keep original failures and deadlines rather than relabeling the original run successful. A proof workflow must itself have reviewed source, normal protected-main delivery and actual execution evidence. Its success does not prove downstream registry reconciliation or whole Delivery acceptance.

The repaired transport uses one bounded HTTPS-only curl GET per stage, disables curlrc, passes credentials through escaped stdin, validates the initial package-base origin, and keeps cross-host redirect authentication stripping. Closed phase/status/exit diagnostics avoid retaining headers, service-index URLs, credentials or stderr. Tests exercise the actual transport with inert local TLS and cross-host/downgrade/credential/diagnostic controls. Use an independently retained native artifact and source/checkout join to qualify a real result; this source lesson grants no new retry, publication or runtime authority.
title: Prove original package custody through a separate bounded read-only workflow
